mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2.5% YoY signals inflationary pressures that lead to tighter monetary policy, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.5% does not correlate with subsequent tightening actions by the Fed.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in one month signals a weakening labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 50% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the increase in UNRATE does not correlate with subsequent GDP contraction.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a recessionary environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 50% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or GDPC1 decline does not correlate with subsequent earnings contraction.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month signals a strengthening economy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or INDPRO increase does not correlate with subsequent earnings growth.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals an easing monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 50% of instances despite the positive signal, or FEDFUNDS decrease does not correlate with subsequent easing actions.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in retail sales (RSAFS) by more than 1% in a month signals weakening consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 50% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or RSAFS decrease does not correlate with subsequent GDP contraction.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 in a month signals a strengthening labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or PAYEMS increase does not correlate with subsequent earnings growth.

mechanism_narrative: A joint increase in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) by more than 5% each in a month signals a strengthening economy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both increase > 5% in 1 month
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint increase in HOUST and RSAFS does not correlate with subsequent GDP growth.
